reasoning_traces.think:
The paper introduces a hybrid model combining a high-dimensional Hawkes process with a graph neural network to analyze opinion propagation on social media. The Hawkes process models temporal dynamics using an intensity function λ_ω(t), which includes baseline rates μ_ω, excitation strengths α_{ω,ω'}, and exponential decay kernels φ_{ω,ω'}. This allows modeling how past comment events influence future ones. The GNN component processes hierarchical comment structures, assigning sentiment classifications based on node features derived from the Hawkes intensities and normalized sentiment distributions. These components together enable prediction of comment volumes, sentiment mixes, and structural evolution over time windows. However, the model lacks applicability to sports prediction domains, as it focuses on general social media commentary rather than specific game-related outcomes or player performance. Its reliance on Weibo data further limits external validity to other platforms or cultures. The lack of publicly available code and datasets prevents practical deployment in GSE or GSI systems.
